clue.text: One ranking highly, extremely exceptional, leading in their field — a prize-winning author

parts.note: a nob is a person of high social rank, a toff

indicators.note: extremely asks for the word's extremes, its first and last letters only

parts.note: leading in a field is coming first, written 1ST, which reads as IST

explanation.surface: A tribute to a top-ranked, exceptional leader in their field who has won a literary prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'exceptional', E and L. 1ST, the numeral for first place, is read as the letters IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate of the Nobel Prize, here in literature, is a prize-winning writer.

clue.text: Certainly, a company will be up for this playwright

indicators.note: in a down entry, being up means the whole run of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: certainly as an affirmative reply means yes

explanation.surface: A theatre company keenly agrees to stage a dramatist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be up' turns the whole string YES A CO upwards, giving the Irish dramatist Sean O'Casey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was the Irish dramatist of Juno and the Paycock.

clue.text: Period in which TV detective's missing at the start

indicators.note: missing at the start means the opening letter of the detective's name is dropped

parts.note: Vera Stanhope is the detective in the ITV series Vera

explanation.surface: An episode in which a television sleuth fails to appear in the opening scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera is a long-running British TV crime drama named after its detective; drop her V.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is an age or epoch, a stretch of historical time.

clue.text: Where Nanooklived asone with endless depression

parts.note: as one, run together in the clue as held, means single: the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for depression is cut off

parts.note: gloom is low spirits, a depression

explanation.surface: An Inuit hunter living alone and feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs words together as held: 'Nanook lived as one'. Nanook of the North is the 1922 documentary about an Inuit hunter; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit hunters such as the film's subject built snow-block domed houses on the ice.

clue.text: "The bloody spur cannot provoke him on, / That sometimes anger — into his hide" (Shakespeare, Sonnets)

definitions.text: "The bloody spur cannot provoke him on, / That sometimes anger — into his hide" (Shakespeare, Sonnets)

parts.words: "The bloody spur cannot provoke him on, / That sometimes anger — into his hide" (Shakespeare, Sonnets)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing verb is the one Shakespeare's Sonnet 50 uses for the rider driving his spur angrily into the horse's flank

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare's verse with one word missing, about a sluggish horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sonnet 50 describes the rider who 'sometimes anger thrusts into his hide'; the clue is a quotation to complete, not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb completing the quotation means drives or stabs, as a spur is jabbed into a horse.

clue.text: A hesitant refusal we hear, a French one

indicators.note: we hear says the letters entered match what is spoken, not what is written

parts.note: a hesitant refusal is 'er, no', with er as the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone stammers a reluctant 'no', and the speaker is French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' points back to 1 Across: Annie Ernaux is the French Nobel laureate in literature (2022), and her surname is pronounced like 'er, no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Ernaux, French memoirist, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2022.

clue.text: Brief work you once invested in ruined estates

indicators.note: invested in means the archaic word is put inside the shuffled letters
ruined says the letters of estates are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Money you put into run-down property in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' suggests money put into property, but here it signals insertion; 'ruined' gives ESSATTE. 'You once' is the old pronoun of address.
explanation.definitionFit: The diminutive ending makes it a short piece of prose writing, a little essay.

clue.text: Has unperson strange verbalconstructions?

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the two words are made odd, reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Does a non-person, as in Orwell, speak oddly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' shuffles HASUNPERSON. The clue as held runs 'verbal constructions' together. 'Unperson' is Orwell's Newspeak word for someone erased from record.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of words built around a head noun are grammatical constructions in language.

clue.text: Those who opposed the Confederatesbut support Labourperhaps?

definitions.meaning: ... were supporters of the federal Union in the American Civil War
trade union members are traditionally backers of the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: Unionists fought the South yet back the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held runs words together ('Confederates but', 'Labour perhaps'); 'but' is a link. Labour is the British left-wing party founded with trade union backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Federal loyalists in the Civil War and members of a trade union share the same label.

clue.text: Initially actress Betty returning with name -

definitions.text: Initially actress Betty returning with name -

indicators.note: returning means the two picked letters are read backwards
initially takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star once known simply as Betty, and her stage name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives A and B; 'returning' turns them to BA. Lauren Bacall was born Betty Joan Perske, so the whole clue describes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall, the screen star of To Have and Have Not, was born Betty Perske.

clue.text: Russian monk, foreignprince, and later leader

parts.note: Ras is an Ethiopian title of a prince or duke
Vladimir Putin is a much later leader of Russia

explanation.surface: Three figures from Russian history: a holy man, a royal and a president.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held runs 'foreign prince' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the mystic holy man at the court of the last Tsar.

clue.text: Russian-born French writer, Prince of Novgorod, embracing Spanish painter

indicators.note: embracing means the prince's name wraps around the painter's

parts.note: Alexander Nevsky was the medieval Prince of Novgorod
Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A medieval Russian prince hugging a Spanish artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Irène Némirovsky, author of Suite Française, was born in Kyiv and wrote in French.

clue.text: United quietly in identical hybrid, like Tweedledum and Tweedledee?

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the mixed letters
hybrid signals that the letters of identical are crossed and recombined

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
p is the musical marking piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Joined softly in a cross-bred twin, like Lewis Carroll's matching pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' rearranges IDENTICAL; 'in' puts UP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's twins are exact copies of each other, so they come as a matching pair.

clue.text: Christie's investigator making a return appearance in larceny probe

indicators.note: making a return means the letters found are read backwards
appearance in says the letters show up inside the run of words

explanation.surface: An Agatha Christie sleuth reappears in a theft inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'larcENY Probe' sits ENYP; 'making a return' turns it round. Parker Pyne is a lesser-known Christie detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Parker Pyne is the detective of Agatha Christie's Parker Pyne Investigates.

clue.text: Storehouses in which idiots repose uncomfortably

indicators.note: uncomfortably suggests the letters of the fools resting are sitting awkwardly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Fools lie restlessly in warehouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncomfortably' rearranges IDIOTSREPOSE; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are places where goods or records are deposited for safekeeping.

clue.text: In a word, what all the news is in the New York Times?

definitions.text: In a word, what all the news is in the New York Times?

parts.words: In a word, what all the news is in the New York Times?
parts.note: the paper's motto is 'All the news that's fit to print', which one adjective sums up

explanation.surface: Summing up the New York Times's slogan in one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit to be published in a newspaper describes copy that is acceptable for publication.

clue.text: Drink female swallows, see-first female one that is

indicators.note: swallows tells the female letter to take in the old exclamation, joining it
first places the exclamation ahead of the female letter

parts.note: lager is a drink, a pale beer
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A woman downs a beer, looking first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' points to 1 Across: Selma Lagerlöf, Swedish, was the first woman Nobel laureate in literature (1909). 'swallows' and 'see-first' put LO before F; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Selma Lagerlöf was a woman novelist and the first female Nobel literature laureate.

clue.text: Emma Stonex's characters revealing predicament in revolutionary realms

indicators.note: in puts the difficulty inside the turned-over letters
revolutionary signals the letters of realms are overturned into a new order

parts.note: a plight is a predicament

explanation.surface: A novel's characters show a dilemma in a land in upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives LAMERS. Emma Stonex's 2021 novel The Lamplighters is about three vanished lighthouse keepers; 'revealing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonex's novel follows lighthouse keepers, whose job is tending the lamp.

clue.text: Female one recently giving some yarn to film director Lee

parts.note: a hank is a coil or measure of yarn
Ang Lee is the Taiwanese film director

explanation.surface: A woman hands a skein of wool to a filmmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' points to 1 Across: Han Kang, the South Korean novelist, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2024. 'giving ... to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Han Kang, author of The Vegetarian, was a recent woman laureate in literature.

clue.text: Greek poet, so happy, mostly delirious

indicators.note: delirious signals the letters run wild and come out in a new order
mostly keeps most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An ancient lyricist in a state of feverish joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts HAPPY to HAPP; 'delirious' rearranges SO plus HAPP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho of Lesbos was an archaic lyric poet of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Iolanthe, say, one going after half-hearted lord

indicators.note: going after places the numeral at the end, behind the reduced word
half-hearted means one of the two middle letters of the heart is removed

parts.note: a peer is a lord
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Gilbert and Sullivan's fairy heroine pursuing a lukewarm aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of PEER's middle Es. Iolanthe, in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta, is a fairy who marries a mortal; the House of Peers features in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy of Persian legend, so Iolanthe is an example.

clue.text: E.g. James Agee or Cormac Macarthy, but not, surprisingly, Thomas Lanier Williams

definitions.text: E.g. James Agee or Cormac Macarthy, but not, surprisingly, Thomas Lanier Williams

parts.words: E.g. James Agee or Cormac Macarthy, but not, surprisingly, Thomas Lanier Williams
parts.note: Agee and McCarthy were raised in Knoxville in one southern state, while the playwright named after that state was born in Mississippi

explanation.surface: A roll call of southern writers, with one surprising exclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Lanier Williams is Tennessee Williams, who took his pen name from a state he was not born in.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a southern US state named after the Tennessee River; Agee and McCarthy both grew up in Knoxville.

clue.text: Inspiration seen in 3DTron oddly

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters, the odd-numbered positions of the film title

explanation.surface: Creative spark found in a three-dimensional sci-fi film.
explanation.walkthrough: '3D' looks like three-dimensional cinema but refers to the answer at 3 Down; Tron is a 1982 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry, and a muse is a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Erstwhile London theatre, a location initially at which poor actor received support

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the next word

a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A theatre where a bad actor was propped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alhambra was a Leicester Square music hall, demolished in 1936; 'at which' and 'received' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra in Leicester Square was a famous London music hall and theatre, now gone.

clue.text: Syrian city where master of the Tiger was reportedly bound

definitions.text: where master of the Tiger was reportedly bound
definitions.meaning: Macbeth's First Witch reports a sailor's wife saying her husband, master o' the Tiger, has sailed to this city

explanation.surface: A Syrian destination for a ship's captain in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth 1.3 the witch reports 'Her husband's to Aleppo gone, master o' th' Tiger'; 'reportedly' refers to her report, not a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is the major city of northern Syria.

clue.text: Roosevelt's First Lady?

indicators.note: the 's stands for 'has': the president's name has these letters within it

explanation.surface: A question about a US president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' wants Eleanor Roosevelt; but it is the first woman of Genesis, sitting in rooSEVElt read as roosEVElt.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first woman created was Adam's wife.

clue.text: "The lazy nincompoop, the —— fop, whose life seemed spent in card-and supper-rooms" (The Scarlet Pimpernel)

definitions.text: "The lazy nincompoop, the —— fop, whose life seemed spent in card-and supper-rooms" (The Scarlet Pimpernel)

explanation.surface: A quotation from Baroness Orczy describing an idle dandy.

clue.text: Local fruit growing in a Llaregub lane?

definitions.meaning: a dialect word for the gooseberry
Llareggub, the village of Dylan Thomas's Under Milk Wood, has a lane named after the dialect fruit

explanation.surface: A dialect berry growing along a lane in Dylan Thomas's fictional Welsh village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing in' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional English for the gooseberry, also the name of a street in Under Milk Wood.
